slides.1.title: Tejo: Wines of the Tagus Valley
slides.1.subtitle: Level 2 · Tagus Valley
slides.1.points.0.label: Irrigated by the Tagus
slides.1.points.0.text: The longest river in the Iberian Peninsula (it also flows through Spain), with fertile alluvial plains alongside inland uplands
slides.1.points.1.label: Abundant and high-yielding
slides.1.points.1.text: Historically Portugal's most important high-volume DOC, supplying the Lisbon market with plentiful red wine
slides.1.points.2.label: Modern transformation
slides.1.points.2.text: International varieties (Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah) were introduced after the 1990s, and the region began moving towards quality
slides.2.title: Tejo DOC: Lisbon's Breadbasket
slides.2.html:
Tejo DOC (formerly Ribatejo) extends along both banks of the Tagus (Tejo), from the Spanish border to the estuary east of Lisbon.

🗺️ Geographical zones

  • River valley (Campo do Tejo): alluvial plains with fertile soils, high yields, traditional high-volume area
  • Hills (Charneca): sandstone and clay, drier, higher quality; modern quality-focused wineries are concentrated here
  • Northern uplands: higher and cooler, retaining acidity

🌡️ Climate

  • A mix of Mediterranean and continental, with hot summers (30-35°C) and mild winters
  • Slightly cooler than Alentejo, but drier than Lisboa
  • The Tagus moderates the local climate, bringing cool nights

🍇 Main varieties

  • Red: Castelão・Trincadeira・Aragonez・Touriga Nacional
  • White: Fernão Pires (most widely planted)・Arinto・Sauvignon Blanc
  • International varieties: Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Merlot (labelled as IGP)
slides.3.title: Tejo Valley vs. Hills: Two Wine Styles
slides.3.items.0.label: Campo (river valley plain)
slides.3.items.0.desc: Alluvial soils, fertile, high-yielding. Aromatic Castelão reds and easy-drinking Fernão Pires whites. High volume, value-oriented
slides.3.items.1.label: Charneca (upland hills)
slides.3.items.1.desc: Sandstone and clay, poorer, low-yielding. Touriga Nacional and Syrah show more structure and are the core of Tejo's quality wines
slides.3.items.2.label: Modern quality wines (IGP Tejo)
slides.3.items.2.desc: International varieties such as Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah perform well here, with IGP labelling allowing flexible winemaking
slides.3.items.3.label: New wave of organic farming
slides.3.items.3.desc: More and more Tejo wineries are turning to organic certification, using the valley's natural resources to make more sustainable wines
slides.4.question: What was the old name of Tejo DOC?
slides.4.explanation: The old name of Tejo DOC was Ribatejo, meaning "beside the Tagus". It was renamed Tejo in 2009, which more clearly reflects the geographical core of the region: the wine-producing area along the Tagus (Tejo).
slides.5.question: What is the most widely planted white grape variety in Tejo?
slides.5.explanation: Fernão Pires is the most widely planted white grape in Tejo (and the whole Lisboa region). Aromatic and easy-drinking, with aniseed and citrus blossom notes, it is the backbone of Tejo's everyday whites. It is also among the most planted varieties across Portugal.
slides.6.message: Congratulations on completing the Tejo lesson!
slides.6.keyPoints.0: Tejo, formerly Ribatejo, lies along both banks of the Tagus and was renamed in 2009
slides.6.keyPoints.1: River valley plains (high-yielding) vs. upland hills (quality) give Tejo two very different styles
slides.6.keyPoints.2: Fernão Pires is the most widely planted white variety; Castelão and Touriga Nacional are the main reds
slides.6.keyPoints.3: International varieties arrived after the 1990s, and Tejo's IGP level allows more flexible blending
